messages:
maya: quick heads-up — I pushed a tiny "twilight" quickpack for the customer finetune (LoRA merge). link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TwilightPack
maya: need short int8 vs int4 comparison + tokenizer sanity check before we promote to dedicated staging.
kevin: on it. which base model + merge strategy? any special token mappings we should know about? @maya
maya: base = redwood/neoxt-13b-v2 (customer requested this). LoRA merged using additive merge_strategy, checkpoint tag lora-twilight-2026-03-18. We also added a custom token <CUST_ENTITY> to tokenizer (id 50213). main things to watch: token id shifts, kv-cache compatibility, and quant artifacts.
rana: I can run a quick latency+quality smoke. please paste the eval command you want me to use.
maya: use this minimal run (seq_len 1024, batch 8 to simulate prod latency):
```
ri eval run \
  --pack gs://redwood/evals/twilight-lite-pack.json \
  --model redwood/neoxt-13b-v2:lora-twilight-2026-03-18 \
  --quant int8 \
  --seq_len 1024 \
  --batch 8 \
  --out /tmp/twilight_int8.json
```
maya: and same but `--quant int4` for the other comparison. attach token_map: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TokenMap
kevin: ok. what metrics do we care about? EM / rouge / hallucination rate / p95 latency? also do a quick codegen BLEU since they use code snippets.
rana: will run EM and BLEU and a small hallucination check (QA prompt set of 200 examples). also will capture p50/p95 latency with streaming disabled.
(eval-bot): queued job 6789 for int8 run, started.
(eval-bot): quick result (int8) — metrics snapshot:
```
{
  "dataset": "twilight-quick-200",
  "model": "neoxt-13b-v2:lora-twilight",
  "quant": "int8",
  "EM": "87.2",
  "BLEU_code": "42.1",
  "halluc_rate": "3.8",
  "p50_latency_ms": "82",
  "p95_latency_ms": "210"
}
```
rana: int8 looks promising — EM drop vs fp16 baseline is ~1.3% (baseline 88.5). BLEU drop small. hallucination within customer threshold (<5%).
(eval-bot): queued job 6790 for int4 run, started.
(eval-bot): quick result (int4) — metrics snapshot:
```
{
  "dataset": "twilight-quick-200",
  "model": "neoxt-13b-v2:lora-twilight",
  "quant": "int4",
  "EM": "81.7",
  "BLEU_code": "34.6",
  "halluc_rate": "8.9",
  "p50_latency_ms": "68",
  "p95_latency_ms": "180"
}
```
kevin: int4 EM drop ~6.8% — too large. also hallucination double-digit-ish, not acceptable for customer.
maya: ugh — any tokens flagged in mismatch logs?
rana: I dug into traces. a small subset of prompts show a token-shift where merged tokenizer id 50213 was interpreted as two tokens in some quantized paths. grep of the log:
```
2026-03-18T15:12:03Z ERROR merge_apply.py: token_map mismatch for token_id 50213 -> seen as [50213, 3] after quantized embedding table pack
```
kevin: that explains part of EM drop and hallucination. could be embedding compression rounding in per-tensor quant.
maya: options?
kevin: short term: disable per-tensor embedding quant for that token (patch embedding table to keep fp16 for indices in token_map). medium: per-channel quant+calibration. long: QAT and retrain LoRA with quant-aware simulated rounding.
rana: I'll rerun int4 with per-channel asymmetric quant + exclusion list for the token id. command tweak:
```
ri eval run --pack twilight-lite-pack.json --model redwood/neoxt-13b-v2:lora-twilight --quant int4 \
  --quant-mode per_channel_asym --quant-exclude-tokens 50213 --seq_len 1024 --batch 4 --out /tmp/twilight_int4_fix.json
```
maya: thanks. please also run int8 with kv-cache disabled to test safe latency/cost tradeoffs (some customers prefer correct over slightly faster):
```
ri eval run --pack twilight-lite-pack.json --model ... --quant int8 --kv_cache false --out /tmp/twilight_int8_nokv.json
```
(eval-bot): queued job 6795 and 6796. ETA ~2h for longer runs.
kevin: if per-channel int4 with token exclusion is within <3% EM drop we can consider offering int4 with warning and a fallback to int8 model for higher-accuracy routes.
maya: note for product: customer expects <2% EM drop. will flag as blocker for int4. int8 likely acceptable but let's validate long-context stability (some of their prompts are 6k tokens in prod). we only ran 1k.
rana: acknowledged — will run a few long-context samples (4096, 6144) overnight and post results.
maya: thanks all. leaving links to quickpack artifacts and logs in the folder. once we have long-context and the per-channel int4 results, we can propose routing policy: preferred=int8, fallback=fp16, override=int4 with explicit opt-in.
kevin: sound plan. @mike-sre FYI in case we need to pin capacity for longer runs.
maya: :rocket:"
